audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Moab revolt notice, Ahaziah's injury, Baal-zebub inquiry, Elijah's confrontation, repeated royal arrests, fire from heaven, third captain's plea, Ahaziah's death, and Jehoram succession.

modern.text: After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

original.text: וַיִּפְשַׁ֤ע מוֹאָב֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֥וֹת אַחְאָֽב

verses.restored: Ahaziah fell through lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria and became ill. He sent messengers, saying, Go inquire of Baal-zebub god of Ekron whether I shall live from this sickness.

familiar.text: And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.

modern.text: Now Ahaziah had fallen through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and injured himself. So he sent messengers and instructed them: “Go inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this injury.”

original.text: וַיִּפֹּ֨ל אֲחַזְיָ֜ה בְּעַ֣ד הַשְּׂבָכָ֗ה בַּעֲלִיָּת֛וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן וַיָּ֑חַל וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ לְכ֣וּ דִרְשׁ֗וּ בְּבַ֤עַל זְבוּב֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י עֶקְר֔וֹן אִם אֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: Rise, go up to meet messengers of king of Samaria and say, Is it because there is no Divine in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal-zebub god of Ekron?

familiar.text: But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron?

modern.text: But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, “Go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and ask them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are on your way to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?’

original.text: וּמַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה דִּבֶּר֙ אֶל אֵלִיָּ֣ה הַתִּשְׁבִּ֔י ק֣וּם עֲלֵ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את מַלְאֲכֵ֣י מֶֽלֶךְ שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם הַֽמִבְּלִ֤י אֵין אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּם֙ הֹֽלְכִ֔ים לִדְרֹ֕שׁ בְּבַ֥עַל זְב֖וּב אֱלֹהֵ֥י עֶקְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: Therefore thus says YHWH: From the bed to which you went up, you shall not come down, for dying, you shall die. Elijah went.

familiar.text: Now therefore thus saith the LORD, Thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.

modern.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘You will not get up from the bed on which you are lying. You will surely die.’” So Elijah departed.

verses.restored: The messengers returned to him, and he said, Why have you returned?

familiar.text: And when the messengers turned back unto him, he said unto them, Why are ye now turned back?

modern.text: When the messengers returned to the king, he asked them, “Why have you returned?”

verses.restored: They said, A man came up to meet us and said, Go, return to the king who sent you and tell him: Thus says YHWH, Is it because there is no Divine in Israel that you send to inquire of Baal-zebub god of Ekron? Therefore from the bed to which you went up, you shall not come down, for dying, you shall die.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, There came a man up to meet us, and said unto us, Go, turn again unto the king that sent you, and say unto him, Thus saith the LORD, Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that thou sendest to enquire of Baalzebub the god of Ekron? therefore thou shalt not come down from that bed on which thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.

modern.text: They replied, “A man came up to meet us and said, ‘Go back to the king who sent you and tell him that this is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending these men to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not get up from the bed on which you are lying. You will surely die.’”

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What manner of man was he which came up to meet you, and told you these words?

modern.text: The king asked them, “What sort of man came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?”

familiar.text: And they answered him, He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins. And he said, It is Elijah the Tishbite.

modern.text: “He was a hairy man, ” they answered, “with a leather belt around his waist.” “It was Elijah the Tishbite,” said the king.

verses.restored: He sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty. He went up to him, and look, he was sitting on top of hill. He said, Man of Divine, the king says, Come down.

familiar.text: Then the king sent unto him a captain of fifty with his fifty. And he went up to him: and, behold, he sat on the top of an hill. And he spake unto him, Thou man of God, the king hath said, Come down.

modern.text: Then King Ahaziah sent to Elijah a captain with his company of fifty men. So the captain went up to Elijah, who was sitting on top of a hill, and said to him, “Man of God, the king declares, ‘Come down!’”

modern.text: And Elijah said to King Ahaziah, “This is what the LORD says: Is there really no God in Israel for you to inquire of His word? Is that why you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not get up from the bed on which you are lying. You will surely die.” Jehoram Succeeds Ahaziah

modern.text: So Ahaziah died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. And since he had no son, Jehoram succeeded him in the second year of the reign of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat over Judah.

translation_notes: Ahaziah's fall and illness are not moral proof against disabled, injured, or chronically ill people; the prophetic dispute concerns royal allegiance and inquiry, not the worth of a sick body.
Baal-zebub/Ekron language belongs to ancient Israelite polemic and may not authorize mockery or persecution of other religions.
The fire-from-heaven scenes kill soldiers acting under royal command. They must not become a model for religious violence, police killing, or charismatic displays of power.
The third captain survives by pleading for the preciousness of his life and the lives of his men; this is the chapter's clearest de-escalation thread.
Elijah obeys the messenger's instruction not to fear the captain; prophetic authority still remains answerable to Divine command rather than private escalation.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 1 to justify calling down harm, spiritual intimidation, religious persecution, mockery of illness, or killing state agents sent by corrupt rulers. Center the third captain's plea that lives be precious and the refusal to make prophetic power a spectacle of death.
